The following statements hold.*

1.  *A finite nonempty lattice is representable if and only if it satisfies the finite colored-graph criterion in [f:criterion](#f:criterion). For each candidate graph size the criterion is decidable by a finite test.*

2.  *There is no deterministic Turing machine that, given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice, always halts and decides $\mathcal R(L)$.*

3.  *There is a nonrepresentable finite lattice $L_0$ of minimum cardinality, specified by the finite formulas in [sec:minimum](#sec:minimum). Every finite lattice of smaller cardinality is representable, and $\lvert L_0\rvert>7$.*

4.  *Given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice $L$, it is undecidable whether $L\cong[H,G]$ for some finite group $G$ and subgroup $H\le G$, where $[H,G]$ is the full subgroup interval.

The lattice $L$ is the full congruence lattice of a finite algebra if and only if there is an $L$-colored complete graph $(A,d)$ satisfying all three conditions below.* 1. * If $p\ne q$, then $d(p,q)\ne0$, and $$d(p,q)\le d(p,u)\vee d(u,q)\qquad(p,q,u\in A).$$* 2. * Whenever $a\not\le b$ in $L$, there are vertices $p,q$ with $d(p,q)\le a$ and $d(p,q)\not\le b$.* 3. *For every nonempty edge set $S$, vertices $p,q$ satisfying $d(p,q)\le a_S$ lie in the same connected component of $\Gamma_S$.* *For each fixed $|A|$, these conditions involve only lattice inequalities, finite vertex labelings, and paths.

Representability is semidecidable. Moreover, a total algorithm deciding representability of finite lattice order tables exists if and only if there is a total computable function $b:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that every representable lattice $L$ has a graph witness in [f:criterion](#f:criterion) with at most $b(|L|)$ vertices.
